b2-demografia-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Ratkó Children
b2-demografia-01.scenario: At a Budapest museum exhibition on twentieth-century family history, a visitor asks you how many children were born in the mid-1950s and what that generation is called.
b2-demografia-01.prompt: Tell the visitor how many children were born each year in the mid-1950s and what the generation is called.
cues: Say how many children were born each year
Say what the generation is called
b2-demografia-01.target: 1953 és 1955 között évente több mint kétszázezer gyermek jött a világra. Ezt a nemzedéket a köznyelv máig Ratkó-gyerekekként emlegeti.
b2-demografia-01.english: Between 1953 and 1955, more than two hundred thousand children were born each year. Everyday speech still calls this generation the Ratkó children.
b2-demografia-01.canDo: I can explain the historical context and demographic consequences of the Ratkó era in 1950s Hungary.

b2-demografia-02.title: Communicative Challenge: GYES in 1967
b2-demografia-02.scenario: At the same exhibition, a visitor asks you what the child-care allowance (GYES) of 1967 gave to mothers and when they could go back to work.
b2-demografia-02.prompt: Tell the visitor when GYES began and when the mothers could return to their jobs.
cues: Say when GYES came into force
Say when the mothers could go back to work
b2-demografia-02.target: 1967 januárjában lépett életbe a GYES. Három év múltával az édesanyák visszatérhettek a munkahelyükre.
b2-demografia-02.english: GYES came into force in January 1967. After three years the mothers could return to their workplaces.
b2-demografia-02.canDo: I can explain the significance of the 1967 introduction of the child-care allowance (GYES) in Hungarian social history.

b2-demografia-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Family Support after 2010
b2-demografia-03.scenario: At a university seminar in Budapest, a student asks you what the government wanted after 2010 and what some economists say about housing prices.
b2-demografia-03.prompt: Tell the student what the government aimed for after 2010 and what some economists say about prices.
cues: Say what the government expanded after 2010
Say what some economists say happened to prices
b2-demografia-03.target: A 2010-es évektől a kormány bővítette a családtámogatásokat. Egyes közgazdászok szerint mire a támogatások megjelentek a piacon, az ingatlanárak megemelkedtek.
b2-demografia-03.english: From the 2010s the government expanded family support. According to some economists, by the time the subsidies appeared on the market, property prices had risen.
b2-demografia-03.canDo: I can describe how Hungarian family tax credits, CSOK subsidies and loans work and what researchers say about them.

b2-demografia-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Caring for Two Generations
b2-demografia-04.scenario: At a community centre for older people in Debrecen, a volunteer asks you what the 'sandwich generation' is and what happened to the dependency ratio.
b2-demografia-04.prompt: Tell the volunteer who the sandwich generation is and what happened to the dependency ratio.
cues: Say what the sandwich generation does
Say what happened to the dependency ratio
b2-demografia-04.target: A szendvicsgeneráció tagjai egyszerre nevelik a gyermekeiket és ápolják az idős szüleiket. A Ratkó-nemzedék nyugdíjba vonulásának idejére az eltartottsági ráta romlott.
b2-demografia-04.english: Members of the sandwich generation bring up their children and look after their elderly parents at the same time. By the time the Ratkó generation retired, the dependency ratio had worsened.
b2-demografia-04.canDo: I can analyze the challenges of population aging, the pension system, and eldercare in Hungary.

b2-demografia-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Plans and Reality
b2-demografia-05.scenario: At a youth-research workshop in Budapest, a student asks you how many children young Hungarians would like to have and what delays starting a family.
b2-demografia-05.prompt: Tell the student how many children young people would like and what the surveys say about their thirties.
cues: Say how many children they want
Say where many couples still live in their mid-thirties
b2-demografia-05.target: A kutatások szerint a fiatalok átlagosan körülbelül két gyermeket szeretnének. Mire a harmincas éveik közepére érnek, sok pár még mindig albérletben él.
b2-demografia-05.english: According to the research, young people would like about two children on average. By the time they reach their mid-thirties, many couples still live in rented flats.
b2-demografia-05.canDo: I can summarize contemporary sociological findings on how young Hungarians balance education, career, and family planning.

b2-demografia-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Family History in Three Steps
b2-demografia-consolidation.scenario: At the end of the exhibition in Budapest, a visitor asks you to sum up Hungarian family history from the 1950s to the present in a few sentences.
b2-demografia-consolidation.prompt: Name the 1950s generation, the 1967 benefit and the role of families in caring for the old.
cues: Name the large generation of the 1950s
Say who looks after the old, according to sociologists
b2-demografia-consolidation.target: Az 1950-es években a Ratkó-gyerekek nagy nemzedéke született. 1967-ben bevezették a GYES-t. A szociológusok szerint az idősek gondozásában nagy szerepe van a családi szolidaritásnak.
b2-demografia-consolidation.english: The large generation of the Ratkó children was born in the 1950s. GYES was introduced in 1967. According to sociologists, family solidarity plays a large part in caring for the old.
b2-demografia-consolidation.canDo: I can recount the trajectory of Hungarian demographic history from the 1950s Ratkó era and 1967 GYES to contemporary family policy.
